BiblicalUsage: Ijon was a city of Naphtali that two kings smote in turn. In 1 Kings 15:20 Benhadad smites Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-beth-maachah, in 2 Kings 15:29 Tiglath-pileser takes Ijon, and Abel-beth-maachah, and Janoah, and carries them captive to Assyria, and in 2 Chronicles 16:4 Benhadad's captains smite Ijon again.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Ijon is the picture of a border town caught between empires: smitten by Syria, taken by Assyria, and named in the record every time.
RelatedPeople: Ben-hadad, King of Syria; Tiglath-Pileser, King of Assyria
